title: Kummer sequences and affine Picard torsion commute with algebraically closed base change
statement: Let $k\subseteq k'$ be an extension of algebraically closed fields [def-sc-field-extension], let $C$ be a smooth separated connected curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves], and let $n\geq1$ be prime to $\operatorname{char}k$. Write $\pi:C_{k'}\to C$ for the base-change morphism and let $c:\pi^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,C}\to\mathbf G_{m,C_{k'}}$ be the comparison map adjoint to pullback of units; let $c|_{\mu_n}:\pi^{-1}\mu_{n,C}\to\mu_{n,C_{k'}}$ be its restriction. Then $(c|_{\mu_n},c,c)$ is a morphism of short exact Kummer sequences [def-sc-kummer-sequence] for $C$ and $C_{k'}$, and the maps of the resulting Kummer long exact sequences are $H^q(c|_{\mu_n})\circ\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,\mu_n)$ and $H^q(c)\circ\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,\mathbf G_m)$ (with the evident analogous map on the final $\mathbf G_m$ term). In degree zero the latter is pullback of global units [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-degree-zero]. Under [lem-sc-h1-gm-pic-pullback], $H^1(c)\circ\rho^1_{k'/k}(C,\mathbf G_m)$ corresponds to $\mathcal L\mapsto\pi^*\mathcal L$. If $C$ is affine, then pullback induces an isomorphism $\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n]\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Pic}(C_{k'})[n]$.

proof.text: Write $\pi:C_{k'}\to C$; by [lem-sc-base-change-curve] $C_{k'}$ is a smooth separated connected curve over the algebraically closed field $k'$, and $n$ is prime to $\operatorname{char}k'=\operatorname{char}k$. The comparison map $c:\pi^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,C}\to\mathbf G_{m,C_{k'}}$ is adjoint to pullback of units, and it carries $\pi^{-1}\mu_{n,C}$ into $\mu_{n,C_{k'}}$ and commutes with $t\mapsto t^n$ because $t\mapsto t^n$ commutes with every ring homomorphism (elementary). The source sequence $0\to\pi^{-1}\mu_{n,C}\to\pi^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,C}\to\pi^{-1}\mathbf G_{m,C}\to0$ is exact by [lem-sc-kummer-exact] for $C$ and clause 1 of [lem-weil-pbc-pullback-cohomology-long-exact-ladder]; the target Kummer sequence of $C_{k'}$ is exact by [lem-sc-kummer-exact] for $C_{k'}$. Hence $(c|_{\mu_n},c,c)$ is a morphism of short exact sequences of abelian sheaves on $(C_{k'})_{\Et}$. Clause 3 of the ladder makes $\rho^q_{k'/k}$ a morphism from the Kummer long exact sequence of $C$ to that of the pulled-back sequence (commuting with $H^q$ of the sheaf maps and with the connecting maps), and the $\delta$-functor property of $H^q((C_{k'})_{\Et},-)$ as right derived functors of $\Gamma(C_{k'},-)$ [lem-weil-pbc-right-derived-universal-delta-functor] makes $H^q(c|_{\mu_n}),H^q(c),H^q(c)$ a morphism from the long exact sequence of the pulled-back sequence to that of the Kummer sequence of $C_{k'}$. Composing, the maps $H^q(c|_{\mu_n})\circ\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,\mu_n)$ and $H^q(c)\circ\rho^q_{k'/k}(C,\mathbf G_m)$ form a morphism of long exact sequences. In degree zero, clause 2 of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-degree-zero] identifies $\rho^0$ with pulling back global sections, so $H^0(c)\circ\rho^0$ is pullback of global units; the $H^1$ Picard interpretation is [lem-sc-h1-gm-pic-pullback] for $u=\pi$. Finally [lem-sc-brauer-zero-all-curves] applies to both $C$ and $C_{k'}$, so [lem-sc-kummer-les] applies to both long exact sequences.

proof.text: Assume $C$ is affine. Choose a smooth compactification $\overline C$ and boundary $S=\overline C\setminus C$, and fix $P_0\in S$. The compactification, boundary, pullback of the divisor line bundles, and compatibility of the quotient presentations with the Jacobian base-change map are exactly [lem-sc-pic-affine-base-change-compatibility]. Thus the map on Picard groups is the map between $G/\Lambda$ and $G'/\Lambda'$ induced by $G=J_{\overline C}(k)\to G'=J_{\overline C_{k'}}(k')$, and it carries $\Lambda$ isomorphically to $\Lambda'$. Clause (d) of [thm-av-final] makes multiplication by $n$ surjective on $G$ and $G'$, while clause (c) gives an isomorphism $G[n]\xrightarrow{\sim}G'[n]$. Apply [lem-sc-divisible-quotient-torsion] to both pairs $(G,\Lambda)$ and $(G',\Lambda')$: naturality of the quotient maps and of $\delta(g+\Lambda)=ng+n\Lambda$ makes their exact sequences a commutative diagram. Its left and right vertical maps are isomorphisms, so the middle map is an isomorphism by exactness (or the short five lemma), namely $\operatorname{Pic}(C)[n]\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Pic}(C_{k'})[n]$.
